newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt traces T-bond amid tight spreads.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt traces T-bond amid tight spreads.

text.p: Emerging market debt tracked U.S. Treasuries Thursday as the summer doldrums and exceedingly tight spreads kept investors from taking on larger positions, Brady bond traders said.
The Brady bond market could not capture much momentum when the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond closed unchanged to yield 6.56 percent.
"After yesterday's important news coming out of Brazil there was not much to drive the market," said Kurt Schmid, managing director at SBC Warburg. "The market took a pause."
News that Brazil's government had defeated an opposition attempt to sink its civil service bill boosted the Brazilian debt, but even these gains were subdued.
Brazilian Cs bonds gained 1/4 to 83-1/2 and the country's global bond due 2027 rose 1/4 to 99-1/2.
What trade there was took place between Wall Street players, dealers said. "Nothing happened today," one Brady dealer said. "It's all dealer trading through the screens."
Dealers said the market would likely need to give back some of its tremendous gains before it could build more upward momentum, for U.S. institutions would find the current levels too costly.
The other main Latin nations tracked Treasuries step by step. Argentina FRBs and Mexican Discounts MXFLL19=RR were unchanged at 94-7/8 and at 94-1/2.
